The public may watch the meeting live on the city’s cable channel MPKTV (AT&T U-verse, channel 99

http://www.montereypark.ca.gov/133/City-Council-Meeting-Videos.

PUBLIC PARTICIPATION
In accordance with Government Code § 54953(e) and City Council resolution, remote public participation
is allowed in the following ways:

Via Email (Written Communications)
Public comment will be accepted up to 24 hours before the meeting via email to
mpclerk@montereypark.ca.gov. Written communications (if any) will be briefly summarized and include
the name of each individual that submitted a comment; the summary will be read via prerecorded video
and played during the Public Comment section of the City Council meeting. To view the full text of written
communications, please visit www.montereypark.ca.gov/AgendaCenter. All written communications are
provided to the City Council and filed as part of the City’s administrative record.

Via Telephone
Public comment may be submitted via telephone during the meeting, before the close of public comment,
by calling (888) 788-0099 or (877) 853-5247 and entering Zoom Meeting ID: 289 222 5995 then press
pound (#). When prompted to enter participation ID number press pound (#) again. If participants would
like to make a public comment they will enter “*9” then the Clerk’s office will be notified, and you will be

Participants are encouraged to join the meeting 15 minutes before the start of the meeting. You may
speak up to 5 minutes on Agenda item. Speakers will not be allowed to combine time. The Mayor and
City Council may change the amount of time allowed for speakers. As part of the virtual meeting
protocols, anonymous persons will not be allowed to provide public comment.

Important Disclaimer
When a participant calls in to join the meeting, their name and/or phone number will be visible to all
participants. Note that all public meetings will be recorded.

 SUBJECT:  Resolution Authorizing the City Manager, or Designee, to Apply for,
  Submit applications, Receive and Appropriate Grant Funds from the SB
  1383 Local Assistance Grant Program

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Adopting a Resolution authorizing the City Manager, or designee, to apply for,
  submit applications, receive and appropriate grant funds from CalRecycle’s SB
  1383 Local Assistance Grant Program on behalf of the City; and
  2. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
CalRecycle requires all jurisdictions to adopt a resolution that authorizes the City or
designee to submit applications and execute documents related to the administration of
CalRecycle grants. The City proposes to submit an application for the SB 1383 Local
Assistance Grant Program. The City would receive approximately $80,214 from the state
for assistance in the implementation of SB 1383 regulations.

BACKGROUND:
Pursuant to Public Resources Code sections 48000 et seq., the California Department of
Resources Recycling and Recovery (CalRecycle) administers various grant programs in
furtherance of the State of California’s efforts to reduce, recycle and reuse solid waste
generated in the state thereby preserving landfill capacity and protecting public health
and safety and the environment. Beginning with fiscal year 2021-22, CalRecycle is
administering a one-time grant program to aid in the implementation of regulation
requirements associated with SB 1383.

The Resolution authorizes the City to submit an application for the CalRecycle SB 1383
Local Assistance Grant Program and designates the City Manager as Signature Authority
to execute all documents related to the program. Funding would be used to implement
SB 1383 requirements, including education and outreach and the expansion of the
regional Food Recovery Program.

 SUBJECT:  Purchase of Utility Truck for Water Division

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Waiving bidding requirements pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code §
  3.20.050 (4) and authorizing the purchase of a Ford F-650 Utility Truck through a
  Sourcewell Contract with National Auto Fleet Group;
  2. Appropriating $173,500 in Water Operations Funds for the vehicle purchase; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The Water Division is proposing to replace a utility vehicle that has exceeded its useful
service life with a Ford F-650 Utility Truck. Staff is recommending purchase of the
replacement truck through a cooperative purchase agreement with National Auto Fleet
Group. An appropriation of $173,500 is requested for this purchase.

BACKGROUND:
The Water Division is proposing to replace a 2006 utility truck that has over 90K miles
and has recurring transmission and overheating problems. The vehicle was towed on
multiple occasions causing undue delays to critical activities in the field such as water
main leak repairs.

The proposed replacement vehicle is a 2022 Ford F-650 utility truck that will be equipped
with accessories that are necessary for day-to-day operations of the Water division. The
options include reinforced lifting capacity for cranes, watt power inverter to operate power
tools, power take off system for jack hammering (which eliminates the need for use of a
compressor), ergonomically designed storage for all tools and equipment for safety and
efficiency.

Staff researched alternative fuel options including diesel and compressed natural gas
(CNG) engines. Locally, CNG fueled utility vehicles are only being offered as an
aftermarket addition at an additional cost between $30K to $40K. Diesel fueled vehicles
are subject to additional California fleet requirements including mandatory diesel emission

control (DEC) strategies. DEC Strategies require a fuel regeneration process that renders
the vehicle inoperable for a period of time, which may interrupt the City’s day-to-day
operations, limiting staff’s ability to complete critical activities. Diesel-powered heavy-duty
vehicles are also subject to South Coast Air Quality Management District’s (SCAQMD)
Rule 1196 and require special approval prior to purchase. Staff is committed to research
and recommend alternative fuel vehicles when feasible. However, in this specific
circumstance and due to the limitations of diesel vehicles, increased costs for a CNG
fueled vehicle, and the City’s poor experience with aftermarket retrofitted vehicles, staff
is recommending purchasing the Ford F-650 Utility Truck with a conventional gasoline
fuel system. The vehicle would comply with SCAQMD Rule 1196, which aims at reducing
air toxic and criteria pollutant emissions. Additionally, since California’s current vehicle
emission standards for new vehicles are higher than in previous decades, the proposed
new F650 utility truck will operate much cleaner than the City’s current 2006 gas-fueled
utility truck.

The City of Monterey Park is member of Sourcewell, a government agency that combines
the purchasing power of multiple agencies into a cooperative purchasing group in order
to solicit lower prices than what a smaller agency may obtain through an individual bid.
Sourcewell contracts are competitively solicited and meet the public bidding process.
Sourcewell is offering the purchase of the 2022 F-650 vehicle through a contract with
National Auto Fleet Group (Contract 060920-NAF). The cost to purchase and outfit this
vehicle is $173,460.09.

An appropriation of $173,500 for the cost of the replacement vehicle is requested from
the water operations fund 401.

  DATE: February 2, 2022
  AGENDA ITEM NO: Consent Calendar No. 3D

TO:  The Honorable Mayor and City Council
FROM:  Frank A. Lopez, Director of Public Works / City Engineer
SUBJECT:  Purchase of Hydro Jet Sewer Excavator Truck (Vactor)

RECOMMENDATION:
It is recommended that the City Council consider:
  1. Waiving bidding requirements pursuant to Monterey Park Municipal Code §
  3.20.050 (4) and authorizing the purchase of a 2022 CNG Vactor Truck through a
  Sourcewell Contract with Haaker Equipment Company;
  2. Appropriating $552,466 for the purchase of the vehicle from the City’s Sewer
  Collection Fund; and
  3. Taking such additional, related, action that may be desirable.

EXECUTIVE SUMMARY:
The South Coast Air Quality Management District (SCAQMD) is requiring the City to
replace a heavy-duty service vehicle from the City’s fleet per SCAQMD Rule 1196,
Clean On-Road Heavy-Duty Public Fleet Vehicles. The vehicle to be replaced is unit #
113, a diesel powered Vactor hydro jet-rodder. This vehicle is used daily to clean City
sewer lines from the street via manholes.

Staff recommends the replacement vehicle be purchased through a Sourcewell
cooperative purchase agreement with Haaker Equipment Company. An appropriation of
$552,466 from the Sewer Fund is requested for this purchase.

BACKGROUND:
The City of Monterey Park was notified by the South Coast Air Quality Management
District (SCQAMD) in May of 2021 that vehicle unit #113 was deemed out of
compliance per SCAQMD Rule 1196. This is primarily due to the vehicle having a diesel

  BE IT RESOLVED by the Council of the City of Monterey Park as follows:

SECTION 1: The City Council finds as follows:

  A. The Supreme Court of the United States acknowledged in its 1973 landmark
  decision Roe v. Wade that the ability to make a private medical decision impacting
  one’s reproductive health is a constitutionally protected right.

  B. Before 1973, the year when Roe v. Wade was enacted, women faced significant
  obstacles to safe reproductive health services, resulting in widespread loss of life
  and severe illness.

  C. In 2002, California enacted the Reproductive Privacy Act, which makes the
  fundamental right to choose to bear a child or choose and obtain an abortion the
  official public policy of the State of California.

  D. The restrictions and bans that violate reproductive freedom disproportionately
  impact populations that already face barriers to accessing care, including the most
  marginalized women: low-income women, women of color, immigrant women, and
  young women.

  E. Access to abortion continues to be a right in name only, with many unable to
  access the medical procedure due to restrictive laws, financial hardships, and
  other barriers.

  F. As States around the country enact harsh laws that violate the fundamental rights
  of people, the City of Monterey Park will continue to uphold everyone’s equality
  and liberty by protecting their reproductive freedom, educating residents about
  their rights to reproductive freedom, to fully exercise their reproductive rights and
  acting as a model for other cities that want to uphold complete reproductive
  freedom for all.

  G. Those seeking abortion and other reproductive care in Monterey Park have the
  fundamental right of privacy for personal reproductive decisions. The right to
  privacy includes a women’s right to choose.

  H. The City Council affirms its commitment to the reproductive freedom rights
  afforded to all women as essential to the lives, liberties, health, and equality of
  women regardless of socioeconomic, ethnic, racial, cultural or religious
  background, age or sexual orientation, and to opposing any laws or regulations
